DERIVATION is core model s3 pattern 1: data/spain_2012_reality.do reads DA2973 by infix with the CIS variable names lowercased ('p3701 141 ... p3710 150', matching ES2973's DATA LIST 'P3701 141 ... P3710 150') and Bookmark 10: personality loops gen item = the literal names p3701..p3710, so the IRW item code IS the CIS variable name; nothing positional, Step 5b exempt, no verification_/verify_ files written. COLUMN CROSS-CHECK: three level-1 records agree for all 10 items -- ES2973 DATA LIST positions 141..150; ES2973 VARIABLE LABELS (/P3701 'Le resulta fácil encontrar sinónimos de las palabras' ... /P3710 'Se pone nervioso/a con facilidad'); and the printed questionnaire grid rows with column markers (141)..(150). Labels name the trait, so no two can be swapped without being self-evident. Data coherence: p3708 (stress) and p3710 (nervous) correlate +0.52 with each other and ~0 with the rest; p3703 (names) and p3707 (dates) +0.45. TEXT (text_source=study_materials): item_text is the questionnaire's printed grid-row wording; P.37's shared stem goes in instructions. The questionnaire PDFs are image-only scans; wording was read visually from 250-dpi renders of page 5 (.cache/spain_2012_reality_personality/crop_p37_A_*.png, crop_p37_B_*.png) -- spot-check advisable. Versions A and B print P.37 identically (compared side by side; FT2973 says the versions differ only in P.9, 12, 15, 21, 24, 26, 29). DEVIATIONS / SOURCE OVERRIDES: (1) p3703 ships the questionnaire's 'Tiene facilidad para recordar nombres' where the ES2973 label reads 'Tiene facilidades para ...'; p3707 ships 'Tiene facilidad para recordar fechas' where the label reads '... recordar las fechas'. The other 8 labels match the questionnaire verbatim. (2) Line-break hyphen joined in p3709 ('concienzu-damente' -> 'concienzudamente'). (3) Dropped from instructions: 'P.37' numbering and the interviewer direction '(MOSTRAR TARJETA S).' (sibling precedent). OPTIONS: option_text is the questionnaire's printed list '1. Sí, completamente / 2. Más bien sí / 3. (NO LEER) Ni sí ni no / 4. Más bien no / 5. No, en absoluto'. ES2973 VALUE LABELS (identical on P3701..P3710) agree on codes 1..5 but omit the comma in 'No en absoluto'; shipped the questionnaire's 'No, en absoluto'. TARJETA S (Preg. 37) text layer lists only the four read-out options in capitals (B numbers them 1,2,4,5), consistent with code 3 being unread. RECODE: the .do sets 3 (Ni sí ni no, NO LEER), 8 (N.S.) and 9 (N.C.) to missing, so the live resp set is 1,2,4,5 with a deliberate gap at 3; no option row for 3 is shipped because no live response carries it. No reversal/recode of any item in the .do; stored direction is 1 = Sí, completamente ... 5 = No, en absoluto (lower = more descriptive) for every item. SENTINELS: raw 3/8/9 over p3701..p3710 = 3824/320/162 (4306 of 29620 cells dropped). REBUILD: DA2973 (2962 records, width 392, id = row number) cols 141..150 minus {3,8,9} reproduces the live table exactly: 25314 rows both, 2940 ids both, 0 only-live / 0 only-rebuilt id-item keys, 0 duplicate keys, 0 resp mismatches of 25314 (.cache/spain_2012_reality_personality/rebuild.R). STEP 3b: dictionary Description ('Self-description on cognitive and personality traits') and the .do header ('personality (P3701 to P3710) 1-5 self-description on ten cognitive and personality statements') describe P.37; 10 items, resp 1,2,4,5 match; no mismatch. validate_items.R --table-sets PASS (10 items, resp 1,2,4,5; 40 rows). language=Spanish; translation_source=machine_translation (CIS publishes Estudio 2973 in Spanish only; all _translated columns are English written by IRW; issues-page line owed once live). RIGHTS: applied the existing instrument_rights_register.csv CIS row (verdict allow, all CIS survey years, irw#2381); originator is CIS (items are CIS's own survey statements, not a named published personality inventory). No register row written.
public_note: Codes run 1 = yes, completely to 5 = not at all (lower means the statement describes the respondent better); the unread middle option 3 (neither yes nor no), don't-know and no-answer are stored as missing, so no respondent has a 3; English is IRW machine translation of the Spanish-only CIS questionnaire
